steps.prompt: Adult tickets cost $\$12$ and child tickets $\$7$. A family paid $\$50$ for $5$ tickets. How could you find how many of each they bought?

cards.title: Two ways to solve a system
cards.body: Substitution: solve one equation for a variable and put it into the other. Elimination: scale the equations so one variable has opposite coefficients, then add them. Either way, find the other variable and check both equations.

steps.text: The $y$ terms are $+2y$ and $-2y$: add the equations.
So $x = 3$. Put it into the first equation: $9 + 2y = 16$.

cards.title: Worked example: the ticket problem
cards.problem: Adult tickets cost $\$12$ and child tickets $\$7$. A family paid $\$50$ for $5$ tickets. How many adult tickets did they buy?

steps.text: Let $a$ be adult tickets and $c$ child tickets: $a + c = 5$ and $12a + 7c = 50$.

cards.title: How many solutions? And inequalities
cards.body: Two lines meet once when their slopes differ, never when they are parallel, and everywhere when they are the same line. In an inequality, multiplying or dividing by a negative number flips the sign: $-3x > 12$ gives $x < -4$.
